recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If future users need normative clarification about how duration interacts with collectedDateTime or collectedPeriod, open or apply a separate work-group decision rather than treating it as unfinished FHIR-17526 work.
issue_request: FHIR-17526 asked to extend Specimen.collection so duration can be captured for collections such as 24-hour urine when exact start and end times are unknown; the final Published/Persuasive resolution was to add Specimen.collection.duration, 0..1 Duration, with definition 'The span of time over which the collection of a specimen occurred.'.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 1e39384034 ('GF#17527, GF#17380, GF#17526') added Specimen.collection.duration to the historical specimen spreadsheet with the requested cardinality, datatype, and definition. Later source rework/import commits, including 33b409a4b6 and c69d71aa21, carried that applied element into the current StructureDefinition XML source.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini confirms Specimen is an active resource in the current core build. OO Confluence minutes for July 31, 2018 confirm the same GF#17526 resolution by 4-0-0. Later implementer Zulip discussion is consistent with using duration for multi-hour urine collections and did not reveal a conflicting later decision. Adjacent FHIR-17380 and FHIR-17514 were not re-decided because they concern separate fasting-status and planned elapsed-time requests.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current source/specimen/structuredefinition-Specimen.xml already defines Specimen.collection.duration as 0..1 Duration with the resolved definition, so a source edit would be redundant.

related_jiras.note: Applied in the same 2018 Specimen.collection commit but concerns fastingStatus[x], not the duration element audited here.
